_README: Curated retrieval ground truth. Each question was written FROM a passage
that is actually in the index -- the passage was read first, then a question
it genuinely answers was written for it. Questions invented first and
ground-truthed later encode what you hoped the corpus said.
Ground truth is (book, page range), never chunk_id. Chunk ids do not survive
a re-chunk or a re-ingest, so an id-keyed eval set silently rots into all
misses the first time extraction changes -- which is exactly when you most
need the harness to still mean something. Book title + page span is stable
across everything except the book itself changing.
'book' matches case-insensitively as a substring of books.title.
'pages' is an inclusive [start, end] span; a retrieved chunk is a hit when
its own [page_start, page_end] OVERLAPS the span (not equals -- chunk
boundaries move).
This is a deliberately STRICT metric. A chunk that answers the question well
from a different page counts as a miss, so absolute hit-rate understates
real quality. That is fine: the harness exists to detect regressions between
two runs over the same corpus, not to publish an absolute score.
The mix is intentional -- roughly a third of these turn on a rare literal
token (Epaphras, Belshazzar, 'husbandman', 'nephews'), which is where the
lexical leg should earn its place, and the rest are paraphrases, where it
should not. A set of only one kind cannot tell you whether hybrid helps.
